title: Displayed Single Sentence

illustrates.quote: Blocked paragraphs are blocked at the adjusted left margin; indented paragraphs begin 2 cells to the right of the adjusted left margin.

blocks.text: In the third person, the correct form is doesn’t, whether the subject is singular or plural.
Cathy (doesn’t, don’t) like movies with sad endings.
blocks.features: Displayed single sentence, indented, set off by blank lines above and below; both 'doesn't' and 'don't' italicized within the parenthetical choice.

blocks.text: The correct form is doesn’t: Cathy doesn’t like movies with sad endings.

print.notes: The section's own running rule text (9.2.2e, on the page immediately before) discusses *multiple* displayed sentences; this example itself shows a single displayed sentence blocked at the adjusted left margin (cell 3) -- both its own line and its runover at the same indent (first==runover), the defining feature of clause d's 'blocked' variant rather than 'indented'.
print.printFeatures: Plain (unboxed) worked-example text; italics used for the emphasized word 'doesn't'/'don't' throughout.

braille.notes: Measured fixed left margin = 0 (no page-layout ASCII padding to strip). Lines 1-3: lead-in paragraph, cell 1. Line 4: blank. Lines 5-6: the displayed sentence -- FIRST and RUNOVER at the same cell-3 indent (blocked, per 9.2.2d, not indented). Line 7: blank. Lines 8-9: closing paragraph, cell 1.

resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines`, verified independently byte-for-byte against references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt lines 6607-6615 (margin 0, confirmed by direct byte inspection: no leading ASCII-space run on any line). The two runs disagreed only on `illustrates.rule`: A cited 9.2.2e ('multiple displayed sentences...as a list'), B quoted the whole of 9.2.2. Neither fits exactly -- this example shows a SINGLE sentence (not 'multiple', ruling out 9.2.2e, which Example 9-4 illustrates instead with its own two-item list) with first-line and runover at the identical cell-3 indent, i.e. genuinely 'blocked' rather than 'indented' -- the specific distinction drawn by clause 9.2.2d. Resolved to 9.2.2d on that direct evidence from the agreed `braille.lines` (lines 5-6 above), not by picking either run's stated id.
